planning_scheme.name: South Burnett Regional Council Planning Scheme 2017
planning_scheme.notes: Every page footer reads "South Burnett Regional Council Planning Scheme | Effective from 28 October 2024 (Version 2.0)". Appendix 2 Table AP2.1 lists v2.0 as a Major Amendment adopted 16 October 2024 and effective 28 October 2024. The scheme commenced on 2 October 2017 (Government Gazette No. 31, 29 September 2017). The council site returned 403 on 2026-10-22, so we could not re-check online that v2.0 is still current; the PDF was downloaded earlier. QHC: the scheme does not mention the Queensland Housing Code (no match for "Housing Code"/"QHC" across all 320 pages), so there is no adoption statement.

qdc_qhc_relationship.summary: Under s1.6 the scheme regulates building work under ss32 and 33 of the Building Act 1975 "through Part 5". The building assessment provisions in the scheme are those in Table 1.6.1, which lists only the bushfire prone area designation. No zone-code setback is identified as a QDC/s33 alternative boundary clearance provision. Table 5.7.1 (Building work) regulates only building work on local heritage places. Class 10 siting therefore defaults to QDC MP1.1/MP1.2, except where a zone-code AO applies through a material change of use for a dwelling house that is ADSR or code assessable. The QHC is not mentioned.

quotes.text: (3) This planning scheme, through Part 5, regulates building work in accordance with sections 32 and 33 of the Building Act 1975.

Editor’s note—the Building Act 1975 permits planning schemes to: ... specify alternative boundary clearance and site cover provisions for Class 1 and 10 structures under section 33 of the Building Act 1975.

(4) The building assessment provisions in this planning scheme are identified in Table 1.6.1. || Table 1.6.1–Building Assessment Provisions | Building Assessment Provision | Planning Scheme Part || Bushfire prone areas || Designation of bushfire prone areas | In accordance with section 32(a) of the Building Act 1975 and section 7 of the Building Regulation 2021, this planning scheme designates the following layers of the Overlay Map OM2.1 to Overlay Map OM2.7 to constitute the bushfire prone area for the Building Code of Australia and Queensland Development Code: (a) Very high potential bushfire intensity; (b) High potential bushfire intensity; (c) Medium potential bushfire intensity; and (d) Potential impact buffer.

definitions.text: Dwelling house | A residential use of premises involving: (a) 1 dwelling for a single household and any domestic outbuildings associated with the dwelling; or (b) 1 dwelling for a single household, a secondary dwelling and any domestic outbuildings associated with either dwelling.
Domestic outbuilding | Non-habitable Class 10a building that is— (a) a shed, garage and carport; and (b) Ancillary to a residential use carried out on the premises where the building is.

Setback | For a building or structure, means the shortest distance, measured horizontally, between the outermost projection of the building or structure to the vertical projection of the boundary of the lot where the building or structure is.
Secondary dwelling | A dwelling, whether attached or detached, that is used in conjunction with, and subordinate to, a dwelling house on the same lot.

rules.verbatim_text: AO2.5 Buildings are set back at least: (a) 6m from the primary street frontage; (b) 4.5m from any secondary street frontage; (c) 1.5m from side boundaries; and (d) 6m from rear boundaries.
rules.notes: Table 5.5.1: a dwelling house is accepted development (no requirements) unless it is in the Bunya Mountains Precinct. There it is ADSR against Section 4 only, which has no setbacks. Code assessment arises only when the ADSR is not met, and s5.3.3(4)(b) then limits assessment to the subject matter of the failed Section 4 AOs. So this AO rarely, if ever, reaches a dwelling house or its domestic outbuildings. It applies directly to other code-assessable development, e.g. dual occupancy.

local_plan_mechanism.summary: The scheme has no local plans (Part 7 contains overlays only). Two zone precincts exist: the Bunya Mountains Precinct (Low density residential), which has no setback AOs in Section 4, and the RU1 Winery Precinct (Rural, Moffatdale), which has a reconfiguring-a-lot PO only. The scheme also has the PC2 Private Hospital Precinct (Principal centre zone), where dwelling houses are not listed.

open_questions: Do the "Small lot dwelling houses" setbacks (LDR AO12.1-12.3, MDR AO20.1-20.3: "For houses on lots less than 400m2") reach detached Class 10a domestic outbuildings or only the house? The Dwelling house definition includes domestic outbuildings.

LDR AO2.5 and RR AO1.3 ("Buildings") reach a dwelling house only through code assessment, which s5.3.3(4)(b) appears to limit to the failed ADSR matters. Should they be treated as applying to Class 10 in practice?

Planning Regulation 2017 Sch 6 Pt 2 s2 limits when a planning scheme can make a dwelling house assessable. Check whether the Table 5.5.2 trigger (lot < 400 m2) and the secondary-dwelling triggers are effective.
Rural AO1.1 depends on road hierarchy ("collector or higher order road"), which is not defined in SC1. A road hierarchy source is needed.
